captions.instagram:
How does the skin work?

Your skin is your largest organ: about 2 square metres that keeps water in, germs out and your core at 37 °C. Cut open a block of it, follow a cell from birth to flake, sweat through a humid heatwave, feel with five kinds of sensor, and see why skin comes in every shade.

→ Your skin is your largest organ: about 2 square metres and 4 kilograms.
→ Pull it apart: a thin epidermis on top, a tough dermis full of vessels and nerves, then fat.
→ The skin you touch is dead: cells born at the bottom rise, flatten and die into a brick wall.
→ Sweat cools only when it evaporates: each gram carries away about 2,400 joules of heat.
→ In humid heat sweat just drips, and above a wet-bulb of about 35 °C even resting in shade can’t cool you.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox-production-fd52.up.railway.app/skinclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: How does the skin work? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
Your skin is your largest organ: about 2 square metres that keeps water in, germs out and your core at 37 °C. Cut open a block of it, follow a cell from birth to flake, sweat through a humid heatwave, feel with five kinds of sensor, and see why skin comes in every shade.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox-production-fd52.up.railway.app/e/skinclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/skinclear

In this video:
• Three layers, one big organ. Skin covers about 1.5 to 2 m² and weighs about 3.5 to 4 kg.
• A wall that rebuilds itself. New cells are born in the basal layer and pushed up.
• Your built-in air conditioner. Vessels widen to dump heat or narrow to save it, and each gram of sweat that evaporates carries away about 2,400 J.
• Five kinds of touch sensor. Merkel cells feel pressure, Meissner corpuscles light touch, Pacinian corpuscles vibration near 250 Hz, Ruffini endings stretch, and free nerve endings pain and temperature.
• Melanin, the skin's own sunshade. Everyone has about the same number of melanocytes; skin tone depends on how much and which melanin they make.
• Healing and what goes wrong. A cut heals through clotting, inflammation, new tissue and months of remodelling into a scar at most 80% as strong.
